events.title: René Descartes is born
events.description: The future philosopher and mathematician was born in La Haye en Touraine, France. He grew up to coin the phrase "I think, therefore I am." He also developed the Cartesian coordinate system.
events.significance: Descartes is often called the father of modern philosophy. His analytic geometry links algebra and geometry, and it underpins much of modern mathematics and science.

events.title: Sir Isaac Newton dies
events.description: The English mathematician and physicist died in London at age 84. He was honored with a state funeral at Westminster Abbey. Dates are given in the modern Gregorian calendar.
events.significance: Newton's laws of motion, his theory of universal gravitation and his work on calculus and optics laid the foundations of classical physics.

events.title: The Eiffel Tower officially opens
events.description: Engineer Gustave Eiffel unfurled a French flag at the summit of his iron tower in Paris. The ceremony marked the opening of the structure built for the Universal Exhibition. At 324 meters (1,063 feet), it was the tallest structure in the world.
events.significance: Once criticized by some Parisian artists, the tower became the best-known symbol of Paris and France. It also showed what iron construction could achieve.

events.title: Daylight Saving Time begins in the United States
events.description: Clocks across the country moved forward for the first time under a national daylight saving law. The measure was introduced as a wartime effort to save energy.
events.significance: The first national daylight saving time began a practice of seasonal clock changes that the US and many other countries still follow.
